# General Layout

## Titles {#sec-Titles}

All chapters should start with `#`.  Subsequent headings would start with more `#`.  For cross-referencing, all chapters and sections can be labelled using `{#sec-NAME}` and then referred to using `@sec-NAME`.  Sections can also be unnumbered by adding `{.unnumbered}`.

For example, this section is titled `## Title {#sec-Titles}` and can be referenced using `@sec-Titles` to display @sec-Titles.

# Sample Chapter {#sec-ChapterLabel}
## Sample Section {#sec-SectionLabel}
### Sample Subsection {#sec-SubsectionLabel}
#### Sample Subsubsection {.unnumbered}
##### Sample Subsubsubsection {.unnumbered}

Chapters, sections and subsections will be displayed in the Table of Contents on the right.

## Font Styles {#sec-Fonts}

The three main fonts are *italic* using `*...*`, **bold** using `**...**` and ***bold-italic*** using `***...***`.

## References {#sec-Ref}

The references should all be placed in the `references.bib` file and laid out in a format similar to BibTex.  The references will be displayed in the References chapter in alphabetical order (even the uncited ones) under the Harvard-Bath referencing style (refer to the [Harvard-Bath referencing document](documents/Referencing.pdf)).

Citations can be made using `@` as `@Rang2012` and the reference will appear as @Rang2012.
